title: Stability collaboration starter kit and decision map
summary: A compact starter kit for cross-team activation of SLOs and reliability experiments. Includes a stakeholder decision map, sprint-level tasks for an 8-week onramp, communication templates, and quick mitigation playbooks for first-line responders.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is designed as a pragmatic starter kit for engineering, product, and operations partners to quickly align on service stability goals. It intentionally favors checklists, small bounded experiments, and clear decision ownership so teams can iterate without long planning cycles.

Scope: 
- Candidate services: hosted-api gateway, model-serving pool (v2), routing/fallback layer
- Focus signals: p95 latency, error-rate (5xx), model-fallback success rate, cache hit ratio
- Timebox: 8 weeks (two 4-week sprints) for initial activation and a 12-week measurement window after rollout

Objectives:
1) Agree on SLO definitions that reflect customer impact (latency threshold tied to region-specific tail latencies).
2) Execute an 8-week activation sprint that produces live dashboards, runbooks, and a rollback policy.
3) Establish a shallow-but-actionable RACI for decisions during incidents and rollouts.
4) Create a communications protocol for cross-functional escalation and customer notifications.
5) Run two small experiments (prefix caching and model-variant fallback) to observe unit-cost tradeoffs.

Stakeholder decision map (who decides what):
- SLO definition & success metrics -> Product manager (PM) + Eng-SRE (final sign-off by Eng-SRE lead if tradeoffs present)
- Rollout policy (canary % thresholds, error budget triggers) -> Platform product + SRE (consensus; SRE has veto for safety)
- Oncall runbook edits -> SRE owner (implements), Feature team provides context
- Customer-side communications -> Customer Success drafts; PM approves

Fast onboarding checklist (week 0):
- Identify service owner and SRE partner (single primary contact each)
- Instrument the three signals above with 1-min resolution metrics (Grafana + tracing tags)
- Create a shared Slack channel and add incident bridge automation (pager/rotation updates)
- Record a short 15-min kickoff recording describing the SLOs and rollback knobs

Sprint plan (8 weeks):
- Sprint 1 (weeks 1–4):
  * Week 1: Finalize SLOs and error budgets; wire metrics to dashboard; baseline measurement begins
  * Week 2: Draft runbooks (triage, mitigation, rollback), create experiment plans for caching and fallback
  * Week 3: Implement safe canary path for fallback; small-scale cache experiment in staging
  * Week 4: Dry-run tabletop incident using new runbook; collect feedback
- Sprint 2 (weeks 5–8):
  * Week 5: Start canary rollout of fallback logic (5% traffic), collect metrics for 3 days
  * Week 6: Increase canary or rollback depending on error budget and tail latency impact
  * Week 7: Evaluate unit-cost changes from caching experiment, document tradeoffs
  * Week 8: Finalize runbooks and handoff to steady-state SRE rotation; schedule 12-week post-rollout review

Communication protocol (templates & cadence):
- Internal incident channel: #sre-service-x-ops with automated bridge and escalation to oncall. Use short-form incident summary template (who, what, when, impact, mitigation in progress).
- Weekly sync: 30-minute cross-functional standup (PM, SRE, infra, CS) to review error budget burn and any experiments.
- Customer-facing updates: CS drafts status page entries for outages only after SRE and PM alignment. For sustained regressions, weekly customer brief until resolved.

Decision thresholds (examples):
- Error budget burn > 20% in 24 hours -> fast pause of non-essential rollouts and an incident review within 2 hours.
- P95 latency increase > 30% of baseline for > 30 minutes -> initiate fallback canary and raise to oncall.
- Cache hit ratio drop > 15% correlating with latency increase -> activate cache warmers / investigate cache eviction policy.

Quick mitigation playbooks (short):
- High tail latency: identify offending host pool via traces, shift traffic to healthy pool, enable model-variant with smaller context window, increase batching timeout to favor throughput.
- Elevated 5xx rate: map to deploys or infra changes in last 60 minutes, rollback immediate candidate deploys, escalate to platform infra if disk/network saturation suspected.

Experiment templates (brief):
- Prefix caching experiment: scope: 10% sample traffic for 7 days; metrics: cache hit rate, p95 latency, unit cost per token; success = >10% cost reduction with <5% p95 latency degradation.
- Model fallback experiment: scope: route 5% of production to 4-bit quantized variant when latency SLO breach predicted; metrics: correctness baseline (BLEU/QA metric), latency tail, error budget impact.

Measurement and dashboards: 
- Minimal dashboard should show: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, error budget remaining, per-route token cost, canary vs prod comparisons.
- Add a simple regression chart: baseline (rolling 28d) vs last 24h to highlight drift.

Risk register (top items):
- Overfitting SLO to noisy signals -> mitigate by smoothing and minimum sample thresholds.
- Customer-facing quality regressions from fallback variants -> require PM approval and validated eval sets before >10% traffic.
- Insufficient observability for new fallback path -> include a pre-rollout observability checklist.

Handoff and steady state: 
- After week 8, SRE rotation owns runbooks and dashboards.
- Product schedules quarterly SLO review with metrics-driven updates.
- Create a lightweight postmortem for any incident that burned >40% of the weekly error budget; link to the SLO playbook.

Open questions to resolve in kickoff: 
- Which evaluation metrics do PM and Research require to approve model-variant fallbacks?
- What compensation policy for billing and customer credits if an SLO is missed? (Finance/Legal input needed)
- Who signs off on enabling automated rollback versus manual rollback for model changes?

Appendix: useful templates (copy/paste)
- Incident short summary:
  * Impact: {describe customers affected, features impacted}
  * Detection: {who/what detected}
  * Mitigation in progress: {actions}
  * Next steps: {owner + ETA}

- Runbook quick checklist:
  * Confirm scope of impact
  * Isolate failing pool or path
  * Activate fallback (if safe)
  * If rollback required, follow the rollback matrix and notify CS

Next steps (immediate):
1) Schedule 45-min kickoff with named stakeholders this week (Renee -> proposed times in Slack)
2) Create initial dashboard and add basic alerts (Eng-SRE infra ticket)
3) Draft canary plan and safe rollback checklist for model-variants

Contact: Renee Kim (SRE lead) — renee.k@redwood.ai

Notes to self: keep playbook short and actionable; the goal is to reduce cognitive overhead for responders and create fast feedback loops between product and operations.
review_notes: This is intentionally lightweight — aim to convert key sections into Confluence templates and a one-slide kickoff for execs. Next revision should attach dashboards links and final runbook snippets.
